summary: This Great Books lecture is already a public spine for Poetry, Stories, and Fictional Heroes: Homer creates civilization by making language, memory, speech, tragedy, and metaphysical access into a shared world people can inhabit.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: A speech is a movie projected onto the world, a war of realities, a narrative that must be remembered so it can be internalized.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The episode read already links this phrase to the public Stories anchor, and the source directly supplies the Odysseus scene used by that lens point.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: If language controls time and space, and poets create language, then poetry is not decoration.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The episode read already links this phrase to the Stories language anchor; the same source also grounds the Poetry page's common-world anchor.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Treat this source as the central dated Poetry mechanism already public: poetry creates civilization by giving a people language, living memory, shared reality, moral formation through tragedy, and metaphysical access to a larger field of meaning.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry owns this source when the active mechanism is language, memory, speech, tragedy, soul-gateway access, and poetic creation as civilizational infrastructure. Stories owns the narrower world-projection and narrative-control mechanism.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the Odysseus/Achilles embassy scene as the constructive story-control case: speech projects an inhabitable world, moves the listener through past/present/future, and fights another reality for internalization.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Stories owns the projection and internalization of an inhabitable world. Poetry owns the broader civilizational medium; Game Theory should not receive this scene unless the player/payoff method is the active question.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep this source as the character-inhabitation bridge: Achilles and Odysseus are in the reader, tragedy makes character and spectator live inside one another, and the Iliad preserves persons as living memory.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Fictional Heroes owns reader-character mutual inhabitation and moral infrastructure. Poetry owns the civilizational medium that makes that inhabitation possible.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as secondary support for civilization as shared inner order: Homer gives Greece common language, memory, heroes, tragedy, and metaphysical access before administration or institutions are the primary question.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Civilization owns the inner-order outcome. Poetry remains the primary concept because the active mechanism is poetic language and living memory creating that order.

new_lens_seeds.title: Poet As Prophet
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: The poet does not merely invent language but channels a larger field of memory, truth, God, Geist, or future speech; poetry then becomes prophecy because its words make future reality speak in the present.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism recurs in this lecture's Shelley close and may connect to later Poetry, Eschatology, Dead World, and Great Books sources, but the current public Poetry page already carries it through the soul-gateway and living-memory anchors.

new_lens_seeds.title: Rhetoric As Temporal World Projection
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Persuasion works by building a sensory and temporal world large enough for another person to inhabit: feast and famine, past promise, present danger, future glory, and emotional reality are arranged until action follows.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The Odysseus embassy scene is strong, but it currently fits the existing Stories and Poetry anchors without a separate public page.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-01-21, this lecture is the main public Poetry chronology point between Great Books #1's book-as-universe premise and the April 2026 Dante poetry-as-invasion material.

The metaphysical language should stay dated and attributed to this Great Books lecture: Jiang compares Geist, collective unconscious, forms, heaven, universal memory, God, and Shelley without turning them into one settled canon doctrine.

next_actions.action: Do not create standalone Homer, Iliad, Achilles, Odysseus, Arete, Eudaimonia, Poets As Prophets, Poetry Portal, Divine Psychic Internet, or Speech Is War pages from this source alone; the public Poetry, Stories, and Fictional Heroes pages already carry the mature mechanisms.

Future public Poetry work should be compression or cross-source routing, not another ordinary append from this source: the page already uses 46 refs from this lecture, carries four direct lens points from it, and remains under size pressure but not split pressure.

If adding episode-to-lens links later, restrict links to precise existing anchors: Stories for world projection and shared language, Poetry for common-world/living-memory/tragedy/soul-gateway mechanisms, and Fictional Heroes for character inhabitation.
